Before relying on that work as audit evidence, the auditor evaluates the expert's competence, capabilities and objectivity; obtains an understanding of the expert's field sufficient to evaluate the work; and evaluates the appropriateness of the work, including the source data, methods and assumptions used, as evidence for the relevant assertion.

citation.ref: Using the work of a management's expert

concepts.subsection: SA 540 (Revised) — Auditing Accounting Estimates
concepts.statement: Accounting estimates sit on a spectrum of inherent risk: some carry low estimation uncertainty and complexity — a straightforward provision computed from a fixed formula — while others, such as an expected credit loss model or a goodwill impairment test, carry high estimation uncertainty, subjectivity and susceptibility to management bias. The auditor's response scales with where an estimate sits on that spectrum: the rigour applied to testing methods, data, assumptions and indicators of bias rises with the estimate's complexity rather than staying uniform across every estimate in the file.

citation.ref: Spectrum of inherent risk

concepts.subsection: CARO 2020 — Clause 3(i)
concepts.statement: Clause 3(i) covers property, plant and equipment: whether the company maintains proper records showing full particulars, including quantitative details and situation, of PPE and intangible assets; whether PPE is physically verified by management at reasonable intervals with discrepancies properly dealt with in the books; whether title deeds of immovable property are held in the company's own name, with details where not; and whether any revaluation was carried out, based on a registered valuer's valuation, with the quantum of change specified where the change is 10 per cent or more of the net carrying value.

citation.ref: Clause 3(i)

concepts.subsection: CARO 2020 — Clause 3(vii)
concepts.statement: Clause 3(vii) asks whether the company is regular in depositing undisputed statutory dues — GST, provident fund, employees' state insurance, income tax and other applicable dues — with the appropriate authorities, stating the extent of arrears outstanding as at the balance sheet date for a period of more than six months from the date they became payable; it separately asks for disputed statutory dues not deposited, with the amount involved and the forum where the dispute is pending.

citation.ref: Clause 3(vii)

concepts.subsection: CARO 2020 — Clause 3(ix)
concepts.statement: Clause 3(ix) covers repayment discipline: whether the company defaulted in repayment of loans or other borrowings, or in payment of interest, to any lender, with the period and amount of default; whether the company has been declared a wilful defaulter by any bank, financial institution or lender; whether term loans were applied for the purpose for which they were obtained, with the amount and details of any diversion; and whether funds raised on a short-term basis were used for long-term purposes.

citation.ref: Clause 3(ix)

concepts.subsection: First Schedule Part I — Clause 3
concepts.statement: Clause 3 of Part I of the First Schedule bars a member in practice from accepting or agreeing to accept any part of the profits of the professional work of a person who is not a member of the Institute. The Council has carved a limited exception for prescribed reciprocal arrangements with certain other recognised professional bodies; outside that carve-out, sharing professional profits with a non-member is misconduct regardless of the non-member's own standing or the quality of the work referred.

citation.ref: First Schedule Part I, Clause 3

concepts.subsection: First Schedule Part I — Clause 4
concepts.statement: Clause 4 of Part I of the First Schedule bars a member in practice from entering into partnership, in or outside India, with any person other than a chartered accountant in practice, unless that person belongs to a professional body the Council has notified as permitted — company secretaries, cost accountants, advocates enrolled with a Bar Council, architects and actuaries among them — subject to the Council's conditions for such multidisciplinary partnerships.

citation.ref: First Schedule Part I, Clause 4

concepts.subsection: Section 143(3)(i) — Internal financial controls reporting
concepts.statement: Section 143(3)(i) requires the statutory auditor's report to state whether the company has an adequate internal financial controls system with reference to the financial statements in place, and whether it operated effectively — a separate opinion from the opinion on the financial statements themselves. MCA notification G.S.R. 583(E) dated 13 June 2017 lifts that reporting for a private company which is a one person company or a small company, or whose turnover is less than ₹50 crore as per the latest audited financial statement and whose aggregate borrowings from banks, financial institutions or any body corporate at any point during the financial year are less than ₹25 crore. The notification as first published put an "or" between those two figures; a corrigendum dated 13 July 2017 replaced it with "and", so both must hold. The exemption is forfeited entirely if the company has defaulted in filing its financial statements under section 137 or its annual return under section 92.

citation.ref: Section 143(3)(i), read with entry 9A and paragraph 2A of MCA Notification G.S.R. 583(E) dated 13.06.2017 (amending G.S.R. 464(E) dated 05.06.2015, issued under section 462) and the corrigendum thereto dated 13.07.2017

concepts.subsection: Companies (Accounts) Rules — Audit trail
concepts.statement: Every company using accounting software to maintain its books must use software carrying an audit trail (edit log) feature that records every transaction, logs every change made to it, and cannot be disabled — mandatory from financial years commencing on or after 1 April 2023. The statutory auditor separately reports whether such software was used throughout the year, whether the audit trail feature operated for all transactions without being tampered with, and whether the audit trail has been preserved as required by the statutory record-retention period.

citation.ref: Audit trail requirement, Rule 3

concepts.subsection: Audit of consolidated financial statements — materiality
concepts.statement: In an audit of consolidated financial statements the auditor computes materiality for the group as a whole, and uses that group materiality to assess whether the permanent and current period consolidation adjustments made by the parent's management are appropriate, and to judge which components are material enough to be scoped in. The principal auditor also computes materiality for each component and communicates it to the component auditor where he believes that is required for a true and fair view on the consolidated financial statements. Materiality for a component's own standalone opinion is computed component-wise on a standalone basis by that component's auditor, for a different opinion, and it does not become the group's materiality.

citation.source: Guidance Note on Audit of Consolidated Financial Statements (Revised 2016)
citation.ref: Materiality in the audit of consolidated financial statements

concepts.subsection: Audit of consolidated financial statements — consolidation adjustments
concepts.statement: Permanent consolidation adjustments are made only on the first occasion of consolidation, or on a later occasion when the shareholding in a consolidated entity changes: determining goodwill or capital reserve, and determining the amount of equity attributable to the minority or non-controlling interests. The auditor pays particular attention to the pre-acquisition reserves and the dates of investment, and to whether pre-acquisition reserves have been allocated correctly between the parent and the minority. Current period consolidation adjustments are made in the period being consolidated and relate mainly to eliminating intra-group transactions and balances — intra-group interest and management fees, unrealised intra-group profits on assets transferred between components, deferred tax on those eliminations, intra-group indebtedness, harmonising different accounting policies, and adjustments for recognised subsequent events.

citation.source: Guidance Note on Audit of Consolidated Financial Statements (Revised 2016)
citation.ref: Permanent consolidation adjustments and current period consolidation adjustments

concepts.subsection: Audit of consolidated financial statements — a component on a different framework
concepts.statement: Where a component prepares its financial statements under an accounting framework different from the parent's — a foreign subsidiary on US GAAP, IFRS or a local GAAP — the parent's management performs the conversion of the component's audited financial statements to the framework used for the consolidated financial statements, and the principal auditor audits those conversion adjustments so that the component's financial information is suitable for consolidation. The alternative route is for the component to report against the group accounting manual, in which case the principal auditor performs procedures to determine that the group accounting policies comply with the GAAP applicable to the parent. On the auditing side, for the parent auditor to rely on and refer to the component auditor's report, the component's financial statements should have been audited under a framework corresponding to Indian GAAS.

citation.source: Guidance Note on Audit of Consolidated Financial Statements (Revised 2016)
citation.ref: Component auditor reporting under an accounting or auditing framework different from the parent's

concepts.subsection: Audit of consolidated financial statements — an unaudited component
concepts.statement: Where the financial statements of one or more components remain unaudited, the auditor reporting on the consolidated financial statements evaluates both the qualitative and the quantitative factors bearing on the amounts left unaudited, and considers a modification of the opinion under SA 705, because sufficient appropriate audit evidence has not been obtained for those consolidated balances. An unaudited component is not dropped out of the consolidation, and an Emphasis of Matter paragraph does not cure missing evidence.

citation.source: Guidance Note on Audit of Consolidated Financial Statements (Revised 2016)
citation.ref: Components not audited — evaluation of a possible modification under SA 705

concepts.subsection: SSAE 3000 — Assurance Engagements on Sustainability Information
concepts.statement: SSAE 3000, Assurance Engagements on Sustainability Information, issued by ICAI, is the umbrella standard for every assurance engagement on an entity's sustainability information, and it covers engagements giving either reasonable assurance or limited assurance. It applied on a voluntary basis to assurance reports covering periods ending on 31 March 2023, and on a mandatory basis to assurance reports covering periods ending on or after 31 March 2024. Assurance on a greenhouse gas statement is dealt with separately by SAE 3410, Assurance Engagements on Greenhouse Gas Statements.

citation.ref: Scope of the Standard and effective date of application

concepts.subsection: BRSR — essential and leadership indicators
concepts.statement: The Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report is mandatory from financial year 2022-23, having been voluntary in 2021-22, and SEBI has started with the top 1,000 listed companies by market capitalisation. It has three sections: Section A, general disclosures about the entity, its products, operations, employees and group companies; Section B, management process and policy disclosures covering governance, leadership and oversight; and Section C, principle-wise performance disclosures against the nine principles of the National Guidelines on Responsible Business Conduct. Section C splits its key performance indicators in two — essential indicators, which are mandatory disclosures, and leadership indicators, which are optional.

citation.ref: Regulation 34(2)(f) read with the prescribed BRSR format, Sections A, B and C

concepts.subsection: Climate-related risks in an audit of financial statements
concepts.statement: Climate-related risks belong inside the auditor's understanding of the entity, and matter more in some sectors than others — banking and insurance, energy, transportation, materials and buildings, agriculture, food and forestry products. Before considering any reference to climate in the auditor's report, the auditor determines whether the entity has appropriately disclosed the relevant climate-related information in the financial statements under the applicable financial reporting framework, because a climate commitment is frequently evidence about an estimate already in those statements — a useful life, an impairment, a decommissioning provision. Where a climate disclosure in the financial statements is of fundamental importance to users' understanding, an Emphasis of Matter paragraph may be warranted; climate narrative sitting elsewhere in the annual report is other information, read for consistency, and carries no opinion.

citation.ref: Ch. Sustainable Development Goals and ESG Assurance — role of the auditor, consideration of climate-related risks

concepts.subsection: SEBI LODR Regulation 18 — audit committee composition and meetings
concepts.statement: Every listed entity constitutes a qualified and independent audit committee of at least three directors, of whom two-thirds are independent directors; where the entity has outstanding superior rights (SR) equity shares, the audit committee comprises only independent directors. Every member is financially literate — able to read and understand a balance sheet, a profit and loss account and a statement of cash flows — and at least one member has accounting or related financial management expertise. The chairperson is an independent director and is present at the annual general meeting to answer shareholder queries, and the company secretary acts as secretary to the committee. The committee meets at least four times a year with not more than one hundred and twenty days between two meetings, and the quorum is two members or one-third of the members, whichever is greater, with a minimum of two independent directors present.

citation.ref: Regulation 18(1) and Regulation 18(2)

concepts.subsection: Section 177(7) — the auditor's right to be heard in the audit committee
concepts.statement: Section 177(7) gives the auditors of a company and its key managerial personnel a right to be heard in the meetings of the audit committee when the committee considers the auditor's report, but no right to vote. Regulation 18(1) of the LODR Regulations separately has a representative of the statutory auditor invited to audit committee meetings when required, while allowing the committee occasionally to meet without any executive of the listed entity present. Under Section 177(8), the Board's report under Section 134(3) discloses the composition of the audit committee and, where the Board has not accepted a recommendation of the audit committee, that fact along with the reasons for it.

citation.ref: Section 177(7) and Section 177(8)

concepts.subsection: Certificate on compliance of conditions of corporate governance
concepts.statement: A listed entity obtains a compliance certificate on compliance with the conditions of corporate governance from either its auditors or a practising company secretary, and annexes it to the directors' report. The auditor's responsibility is the verification and certification of the factual implementation of the conditions stipulated in the LODR Regulations: it is neither an audit nor an expression of opinion on the financial statements, and it is neither an assurance as to the future viability of the company nor as to the efficiency or effectiveness with which management has conducted the company's affairs. The work is carried out under the Guidance Note on Certification of Corporate Governance, with documentation under SA 230 and management representations under SA 580. Facts such as an audit committee that did not meet four times, or a chairman of the audit committee who is not an independent director, call for an adverse or qualified statement in the certificate.

citation.ref: Regulation 34(3) read with Schedule V — compliance certificate on conditions of corporate governance

concepts.subsection: Section 143(6) — CAG supplementary audit of a government company
concepts.statement: In a government company the Comptroller and Auditor-General appoints the auditor under Section 139(5) or Section 139(7) and directs the manner in which the accounts are to be audited; the auditor then submits a copy of his audit report to the CAG, and that copy includes the CAG's directions, the action taken on them, and their impact on the accounts and financial statement of the company. Section 143(6) gives the CAG, within sixty days from the date of receipt of that audit report, a right to conduct a supplementary audit through persons he authorises and to comment upon or supplement the audit report; the comments or supplement are sent by the company to every person entitled to copies of the audited financial statements under Section 136(1) and are placed before the annual general meeting at the same time and in the same manner as the audit report. Section 143(7) separately allows the CAG to order a test audit.

citation.ref: Section 143(5), Section 143(6) and the proviso to Section 143(6), and Section 143(7)

concepts.subsection: SQC 1 — retention of engagement documentation
concepts.statement: SQC 1 requires the firm to establish policies and procedures for the retention of engagement documentation, and in the specific case of audit engagements the retention period is ordinarily no shorter than seven years from the date of the auditor's report or, if later, the date of the group auditor's report. This is a firm-level retention obligation running from a report date, and it is separate from the SA 230 requirement to complete the administrative assembly of the final audit file ordinarily within not more than sixty days after the date of the auditor's report.

citation.ref: para 83 — retention period for engagement documentation

concepts.subsection: Advances — provisioning norms
concepts.statement: Provisioning follows classification. A substandard asset carries a general provision of 15 per cent of the total outstanding, made without any allowance for ECGC guarantee cover or securities available, and an unsecured exposure identified as substandard carries an additional 10 per cent — 25 per cent in all. On a doubtful asset the extent not covered by the realisable value of the security carries 100 per cent, and the secured portion carries 25 per cent where the asset has remained doubtful up to one year, 40 per cent for one to three years, and 100 per cent beyond three years. A loss asset should be written off, and if it is permitted to remain on the books, 100 per cent of the outstanding is provided.

citation.ref: Prudential norms on IRACP — paras 5.2, 5.3 and 5.4

concepts.subsection: Section 212 — investigation by the Serious Fraud Investigation Office
concepts.statement: Under Section 212(1) the Central Government may, by order, assign an investigation into a company's affairs to the Serious Fraud Investigation Office on receipt of a report of the Registrar or an inspector under Section 208, on intimation of a special resolution passed by the company that its affairs are required to be investigated, in the public interest, or on a request from any Department of the Central Government or a State Government. Once a case is so assigned, Section 212(2) bars any other investigating agency of the Central Government or of any State Government from proceeding with an investigation in that case in respect of an offence under the Act; an investigation already initiated is not proceeded with further, and the agency concerned transfers the relevant documents and records to the SFIO.

citation.ref: Section 212(1) and Section 212(2)

concepts.subsection: SA 230 — Audit Documentation
concepts.statement: An auditor complies with each requirement of an SA unless the whole SA is not relevant, or the requirement is not relevant because it is conditional and the condition does not exist. In exceptional circumstances the auditor may judge it necessary to depart from a relevant requirement, and must then perform alternative audit procedures to achieve the aim of that requirement. SA 230 makes the departure visible rather than silent: the auditor documents how the alternative audit procedures performed achieve the aim of the requirement, and the reasons for the departure. The same standard requires the file to record the identifying characteristics of the specific items or matters tested, who performed the audit work and the date the work was completed, and who reviewed the audit work performed and the date and extent of that review.

citation.ref: para 9 and para 12, read with SA 200 para 23

concepts.subsection: SA 620 — Using the Work of an Auditor's Expert
concepts.statement: Satisfying himself about the competence, capabilities and objectivity of the auditor's expert is only the entry ticket. The auditor then evaluates the adequacy of the expert's work for the auditor's purposes: the relevance and reasonableness of that expert's findings or conclusions and their consistency with other audit evidence; where the work uses significant assumptions and methods, the relevance and reasonableness of those assumptions and methods in the circumstances; and where the work uses source data significant to it, the relevance, completeness and accuracy of that source data. If the work is not adequate for the auditor's purposes, the auditor agrees with that expert on the nature and extent of further work to be performed by the expert, or performs additional audit procedures appropriate to the circumstances.

citation.ref: para 12 and para 13

concepts.subsection: SA 510 — Initial Audit Engagements: Opening Balances
concepts.statement: SA 510 separates the two reasons an opening balance damages the current opinion. Where the auditor is unable to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence regarding the opening balances, the opinion is qualified or disclaimed, as appropriate. Where the opening balances contain a misstatement that materially affects the current period's financial statements and the effect is not properly accounted for or not adequately presented or disclosed, the opinion is qualified or adverse. The same qualified-or-adverse answer applies where the current period's accounting policies are not consistently applied in relation to the opening balances, or where a change is not properly accounted for, presented or disclosed. And where the predecessor auditor's opinion was modified and the matter remains relevant and material to the current period's financial statements, the auditor modifies his own opinion on the current period's financial statements — an Other Matter paragraph recording what the predecessor said does not discharge it.

citation.ref: paras 10, 11, 12 and 13

concepts.subsection: SA 710 — Comparative Information: Corresponding Figures
concepts.statement: Where the prior period's financial statements were audited by a predecessor auditor and the auditor is not prohibited by law or regulation from referring to that report, the auditor states in an Other Matter paragraph that the corresponding figures were audited by the predecessor auditor, the type of opinion the predecessor expressed and, if that opinion was modified, the reasons for the modification, and the date of that report. Where the prior period's financial statements were not audited at all, the auditor states in an Other Matter paragraph that the corresponding figures are unaudited. Saying so does not relieve the auditor of the requirement to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence that the opening balances do not contain misstatements that materially affect the current period's financial statements.

citation.ref: para 13 and para 14

concepts.subsection: SA 520 — Analytical Procedures
concepts.statement: A substantive analytical procedure is only as good as four things the auditor must settle before it is run. The auditor determines the suitability of the particular procedure for the given assertions, taking account of the assessed risks of material misstatement and of any tests of details for those assertions; evaluates the reliability of the data from which the expectation is developed, taking account of its source, comparability, nature and relevance and the controls over its preparation; develops an expectation of recorded amounts or ratios sufficiently precise to identify a misstatement that, individually or when aggregated with others, may cause the financial statements to be materially misstated; and determines the amount of any difference of recorded amounts from expected values that is acceptable without further investigation. Where the results show fluctuations or relationships inconsistent with other relevant information, or that differ from expected values by a significant amount, the auditor investigates by inquiring of management, obtaining appropriate audit evidence relevant to management's responses, and performing other audit procedures as necessary.

citation.ref: para 5 and para 7

concepts.subsection: SA 530 — Audit Sampling
concepts.statement: An anomaly is a misstatement or deviation that is demonstrably not representative of misstatements or deviations in a population. The label is available only in extremely rare circumstances, and only where the auditor has obtained a high degree of certainty that the misstatement or deviation is not representative of the population — a certainty obtained by performing additional audit procedures sufficient to provide it, not by accepting management's explanation of the cause. An anomalous misstatement may then be left out when projecting misstatements from the sample to the population, but the misstatement itself does not disappear: its own effect, if uncorrected, is still added to the projected misstatement of the rest when the auditor evaluates the results of the sample.

citation.ref: para 5(e), para 13 and para 14

concepts.subsection: SA 560 — Subsequent Events
concepts.statement: After the financial statements have been issued the auditor has no obligation to perform any audit procedures on them. But if a fact then becomes known that, had it been known at the date of the auditor's report, may have caused the auditor to amend that report, the auditor discusses the matter with management and, where appropriate, those charged with governance, determines whether the financial statements need amendment and, if so, inquires how management intends to address the matter. Where management amends, the auditor carries out the audit procedures necessary in the circumstances on the amendment, reviews the steps management takes to ensure that anyone in receipt of the previously issued financial statements together with the auditor's report on them is informed, and issues a new or amended auditor's report that includes an Emphasis of Matter paragraph or Other Matter paragraph referring to a note that more extensively discusses the reason for the amendment and to the earlier report. Where management does not take those steps and does not amend the financial statements, the auditor notifies management and those charged with governance that he will seek to prevent future reliance on the auditor's report, and if they still do not act, takes appropriate action to seek to prevent that reliance.

citation.ref: paras 14, 16 and 17

concepts.subsection: SA 580 — Written Representations
concepts.statement: The written representations are dated as near as practicable to, but not after, the date of the auditor's report, and cover all financial statements and periods referred to in that report. If management does not provide one or more of the requested representations, the auditor discusses the matter with management, re-evaluates the integrity of management and the effect that has on the reliability of representations and of audit evidence in general, and takes appropriate actions including the possible effect on the opinion. Two situations are answered by a disclaimer of opinion rather than by a qualification: where the auditor concludes that there is sufficient doubt about the integrity of management such that the representations about management's own responsibilities are not reliable, and where management simply does not provide those representations — that it has fulfilled its responsibility for the preparation of the financial statements, and that it has provided the auditor with all relevant information and access agreed in the terms of the audit engagement.

citation.ref: para 14, para 19 and para 20

concepts.subsection: SA 550 — Related Parties
concepts.statement: Where the auditor identifies related parties or significant related party transactions that management has not previously identified or disclosed to the auditor, the response is a set of six steps, not a disclosure edit. The auditor promptly communicates the relevant information to the other members of the engagement team; requests management to identify all transactions with the newly identified related parties for the auditor's further evaluation; inquires why the entity's controls over related party relationships and transactions failed to enable the identification or disclosure; performs appropriate substantive audit procedures on the newly identified related parties or significant related party transactions; reconsiders the risk that other related parties or significant related party transactions may exist that management has not disclosed, and performs additional audit procedures as necessary; and where the non-disclosure by management appears intentional, and is therefore indicative of a risk of material misstatement due to fraud, evaluates the implications for the audit.

citation.ref: para 22

concepts.subsection: SA 501 — Audit Evidence: Litigation and Claims
concepts.statement: The auditor designs and performs audit procedures to identify litigation and claims involving the entity which may give rise to a risk of material misstatement, including inquiry of management and, where applicable, others within the entity including in-house legal counsel; reviewing minutes of meetings of those charged with governance and correspondence between the entity and its external legal counsel; and reviewing legal expense accounts. Where the auditor assesses a risk of material misstatement regarding litigation or claims that have been identified, or where procedures indicate that other material litigation or claims may exist, the auditor seeks direct communication with the entity's external legal counsel through a letter of inquiry prepared by management and sent by the auditor, asking the external legal counsel to communicate directly with the auditor. Where management refuses to give that permission, or the external legal counsel refuses to respond appropriately or is prohibited from responding, and the auditor is unable to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence by performing alternative audit procedures, the auditor modifies the opinion.

citation.ref: paras 9, 10 and 11

concepts.subsection: SA 240 — The Auditor's Responsibilities Relating to Fraud
concepts.statement: Where the auditor has identified a fraud or has obtained information that indicates a fraud may exist, he communicates these matters on a timely basis to the appropriate level of management — ordinarily at least one level above the persons who appear to be involved. Where the auditor identifies or suspects fraud involving management, employees who have significant roles in internal control, or others where the fraud results in a material misstatement in the financial statements, he communicates these matters to those charged with governance on a timely basis. Where a misstatement resulting from fraud or suspected fraud brings the auditor's ability to continue performing the audit into question, the auditor determines the professional and legal responsibilities applicable in the circumstances, considers whether to withdraw where withdrawal is possible under applicable law, and if he withdraws, discusses the withdrawal and its reasons with the appropriate level of management and those charged with governance and determines whether there is a professional or legal requirement to report the withdrawal and its reasons to the persons who made the audit appointment or to regulatory authorities. The professional duty of confidentiality may be overridden by law, and the auditor may take legal advice on where that line falls.

citation.ref: para 38, para 40, para 41 and para 43

concepts.subsection: Section 143(12) with Rule 13 — the mechanics of reporting a fraud
concepts.statement: Where the auditor has reason to believe that an offence of fraud involving, or expected to involve individually, an amount of one crore rupees or above is being or has been committed against the company by its officers or employees, he reports the matter to the Central Government by a fixed route. He first reports to the Board or the Audit Committee immediately but not later than two days of his knowledge of the fraud, seeking their reply or observations within forty-five days. On receiving that reply he forwards his report, the reply or observations, and his own comments on them, to the Central Government within fifteen days of receiving the reply. Where no reply or observations come within the forty-five days, he forwards his report to the Central Government along with a note containing the details of the report earlier sent and not replied to. The report goes to the Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs in a sealed cover by registered post with acknowledgement due or by speed post followed by an email in confirmation, on the auditor's letterhead, signed with his seal and quoting his membership number, in the form of the statement specified in Form ADT-4. Where the fraud is below one crore rupees, it goes to the Audit Committee constituted under section 177 or to the Board within the same two days, stating the nature of the fraud with description, the approximate amount involved and the parties involved, and those details are then disclosed in the Board's report.

citation.ref: Section 143(12) read with Rule 13(1), Rule 13(2) and Rule 13(3) of the Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014

concepts.subsection: Sections 21A and 21B — the Board of Discipline and the Disciplinary Committee
concepts.statement: Which forum hears a case is decided by which Schedule the misconduct sits in, and the Director (Discipline) makes that routing after forming a prima facie opinion on the complaint or information. A case of misconduct falling under the First Schedule goes before the Board of Discipline. A case falling under the Second Schedule, or under both the Schedules, goes before the Disciplinary Committee. The powers differ with the forum. On holding a member guilty under the First Schedule, the Board of Discipline may reprimand the member, remove his name from the Register of Members for a period not exceeding three months, or impose a fine. On holding a member guilty under the Second Schedule or under both Schedules, the Disciplinary Committee may reprimand the member, remove his name from the Register of Members permanently or for such period as it thinks fit, or impose a fine. Permanent removal belongs to the Disciplinary Committee alone, and the Director (Discipline) punishes nobody.

citation.ref: Section 21A(3) and Section 21B(3), read with the routing under Section 21(3)

concepts.subsection: SA 260 (Revised) — Communication with Those Charged with Governance
concepts.statement: Planning communication and findings communication are two different requirements, and the second is a named list. The auditor communicates to those charged with governance his views about significant qualitative aspects of the entity's accounting practices, including accounting policies, accounting estimates and financial statement disclosures; significant difficulties, if any, encountered during the audit; unless all of those charged with governance are involved in managing the entity, significant matters arising during the audit that were discussed with, or subject to correspondence with, management, and the written representations the auditor is requesting; circumstances that affect the form and content of the auditor's report; and any other significant matters relevant to the oversight of the financial reporting process. Significant findings are communicated in writing where, in the auditor's professional judgement, oral communication would not be adequate. None of it is conditional on the opinion turning out modified, and telling management is not telling those charged with governance.

citation.ref: para 16

concepts.subsection: SA 265 — Communicating Deficiencies in Internal Control
concepts.statement: A significant deficiency does not stop at those charged with governance. SA 265 sends it in writing to those charged with governance and, separately and also in writing, to management at an appropriate level of responsibility; other deficiencies of sufficient importance to merit management's attention go to management alone. The written communication of a significant deficiency has a prescribed content. It carries a description of the deficiencies and an explanation of their potential effects, and sufficient information to enable those charged with governance and management to understand the context of the communication — namely that the purpose of the audit was to express an opinion on the financial statements, that the audit considered internal control relevant to the preparation of the financial statements in order to design audit procedures appropriate in the circumstances but not for the purpose of expressing an opinion on the effectiveness of internal control, and that the matters reported are limited to those deficiencies identified during the audit and concluded to be of sufficient importance to merit being reported.

citation.ref: para 10 and para 11

concepts.subsection: SA 402 — Audit Considerations Relating to an Entity Using a Service Organisation
concepts.statement: A complementary user entity control is a control that the service organisation assumes, in the design of its service, will be implemented by user entities, and which is identified in the description of its system if it is necessary to achieve the stated control objectives. It does not sit at the service organisation, so the service auditor never tests it. A user auditor using a type 1 or type 2 report must therefore determine whether the complementary user entity controls identified by the service organisation are relevant to the user entity and, where they are, obtain an understanding of whether the user entity has designed and implemented them and test their operating effectiveness at the user entity. Two further things are evaluated before a type 2 report supports reliance: whether the period it covers is appropriate for the user auditor's purposes, and the adequacy of the time period covered by the tests of controls together with the time elapsed since those tests were performed.

citation.ref: para 8(a) defining a complementary user entity control, with the requirement, when a type 1 or type 2 report is used, to determine whether those controls are relevant and to test them at the user entity

concepts.subsection: SA 330 — The Auditor's Responses to Assessed Risks
concepts.statement: Audit evidence about the operating effectiveness of controls obtained in a previous audit may be carried forward, on conditions. The auditor first establishes the continuing relevance of that evidence by obtaining audit evidence about whether significant changes in those controls have occurred since, through inquiry combined with observation or inspection. Where the controls have changed, they are tested in the current audit. Where they have not changed, they are tested at least once in every third audit, and some controls from the rotating population are tested in each audit so that no year passes with none of them tested. The concession stops at a significant risk: where the auditor plans to rely on controls over a risk he has determined to be a significant risk, those controls are tested in the current period, every period he relies on them.

citation.ref: para 14 and para 15, with the continuing-relevance test in para 13

concepts.subsection: SA 330 — The Auditor's Responses to Assessed Risks
concepts.statement: Substantive procedures performed at an interim date leave a gap between that date and the period end, and SA 330 does not let it stay open. The auditor covers the remaining period by performing substantive procedures combined with tests of controls for the intervening period, or, where he determines that is sufficient, further substantive procedures only — either route having to provide a reasonable basis for extending the audit conclusions from the interim date to the period end. And where misstatements that the auditor did not expect are detected at the interim date, the auditor evaluates whether the related assessment of risk and the planned nature, timing and extent of the substantive procedures covering the remaining period need to be modified. Interim work is a way of spreading the audit, not a conclusion that survives contrary evidence found while doing it.

citation.ref: para 22 and para 23

concepts.subsection: SA 450 — Evaluation of Misstatements Identified during the Audit
concepts.statement: Before the evaluation of uncorrected misstatements begins, SA 450 sends the auditor back to materiality. The auditor communicates on a timely basis all misstatements accumulated during the audit with the appropriate level of management, unless prohibited by law or regulation, and requests management to correct them. Where management refuses to correct some or all of them, the auditor obtains an understanding of management's reasons for not making the corrections and takes that understanding into account when evaluating whether the financial statements as a whole are free from material misstatement. And prior to evaluating the effect of uncorrected misstatements, the auditor reassesses materiality determined in accordance with SA 320 to confirm whether it remains appropriate in the context of the entity's actual financial results. The planning figure was built on an expectation; by the end of the audit the year has actually happened.

citation.ref: para 8, para 9 and para 10

concepts.subsection: SA 701 — Communicating Key Audit Matters
concepts.statement: SA 701 states its own limits. Communicating key audit matters in the auditor's report is not a substitute for disclosures in the financial statements that the applicable financial reporting framework requires management to make; not a substitute for the auditor expressing a modified opinion when the circumstances of the engagement require it under SA 705 (Revised); not a substitute for reporting in accordance with SA 570 (Revised) where a material uncertainty relating to going concern exists; and not a separate opinion on individual matters. It follows that a matter giving rise to a modified opinion, and a material uncertainty related to going concern, are by their nature key audit matters — and that neither is described in the Key Audit Matters section. Each is reported under its own standard, and the Key Audit Matters section carries a reference to the Basis for Qualified (Adverse) Opinion section or to the Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern section.

citation.ref: para 4 and para 14

concepts.subsection: SA 705 (Revised) — Modifications to the Opinion
concepts.statement: A limitation imposed by management after the auditor has accepted the engagement has its own path, and the path does not begin with the opinion. The auditor requests management to remove the limitation. If management refuses, the auditor communicates the matter to those charged with governance and determines whether it is possible to perform alternative procedures to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence. If he remains unable to obtain that evidence, the consequence is graded. Where the possible effects on the financial statements of undetected misstatements, if any, could be material but not pervasive, the opinion is qualified. Where they could be both material and pervasive, the auditor withdraws from the audit where withdrawal is practicable and possible under applicable law or regulation, and disclaims an opinion only where withdrawal before issuing the report is not practicable or possible. Where he withdraws, he first communicates to those charged with governance any matters regarding misstatements identified during the audit that would have given rise to a modification of the opinion.

citation.ref: para 11, para 12, para 13 and para 14

concepts.subsection: SA 570 (Revised) — Going Concern
concepts.statement: SA 570 has three reporting outcomes and they are not interchangeable. Where the financial statements have been prepared using the going concern basis of accounting but, in the auditor's judgement, management's use of that basis is inappropriate, the auditor expresses an adverse opinion — and a full and accurate note does not rescue it, because the basis of preparation runs through every figure rather than through one disclosure. Where the use of the going concern basis is appropriate but a material uncertainty exists and is adequately disclosed, the opinion is unmodified with a separate Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern section; where that disclosure is not adequate, the opinion is qualified or adverse as appropriate. And where management is unwilling to make or extend its assessment when the auditor requests it, the auditor considers the implications for the auditor's report, the question being an inability to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence about the appropriateness of the basis itself.

citation.ref: para 21, para 23 and para 24

concepts.subsection: SA 805 — Special Considerations: Single Financial Statements and Specific Elements
concepts.statement: SA 805 draws a line between a single financial statement and a specific element of a financial statement once the opinion on the complete set has gone wrong. Where the opinion on the entity's complete set of financial statements is adverse, or the auditor disclaimed an opinion on it, the auditor shall not express an unmodified opinion in the same auditor's report on a single financial statement that forms part of those financial statements, or on a specific element that forms part of them, because the unmodified opinion would contradict the adverse opinion or disclaimer. A specific element may still carry an unmodified opinion in a separate audit, on three conditions that must all hold: the auditor is not prohibited by law or regulation from doing so, that opinion is expressed in an auditor's report that is not published together with the report containing the adverse opinion or disclaimer of opinion, and the specific element does not constitute a major portion of the entity's complete set of financial statements. A single financial statement never can, because the standard deems it to constitute a major portion of those financial statements.

citation.ref: para 17, para 18 and para 19

concepts.subsection: First Schedule Part I — Clause 10
concepts.statement: A member in practice is guilty of professional misconduct if he charges or offers to charge, accepts or offers to accept, in respect of any professional employment, fees which are based on a percentage of profits or which are contingent upon the findings or results of such employment, except as permitted under any regulation made under the Chartered Accountants Act. The exception is Regulation 192, which names the permitted cases: a receiver or a liquidator may charge on a percentage of the realisation or disbursement of the assets; the auditor of a co-operative society may charge on a percentage of the paid-up capital, the working capital, the gross or net income or the profits; a valuer for the purposes of direct taxes and duties may charge on a percentage of the value of the property valued; and the Council has permitted a percentage or contingent basis for certain management consultancy services, fund raising services, debt recovery services and cost optimisation services. Anything outside that list is misconduct however the engagement letter dresses it, and the clause reaches every kind of professional employment, not audit alone.

citation.ref: First Schedule, Part I, Clause 10, read with Regulation 192 of the Chartered Accountants Regulations, 1988

concepts.subsection: CARO 2020 — Clause 3(xix)
concepts.statement: Clause 3(xix) makes the auditor state, on the basis of the financial ratios, the ageing and expected dates of realisation of financial assets and payment of financial liabilities, other information accompanying the financial statements, and his knowledge of the Board of Directors' and management's plans, whether he is of the opinion that no material uncertainty exists as on the date of the audit report that the company is not capable of meeting its liabilities existing at the date of the balance sheet as and when they fall due within a period of one year from the balance sheet date. The clause also makes him state that his reporting is based on the facts up to the date of the audit report, and that he neither gives any guarantee nor any assurance that all liabilities falling due within a period of one year from the balance sheet date will get discharged by the company as and when they fall due. It is anchored twice to the balance sheet date — the liabilities are those existing then, and the one-year window runs from then — and it is not the going concern conclusion under SA 570.

citation.ref: paragraph 3(xix)

concepts.subsection: CARO 2020 — Clause 3(xiv)
concepts.statement: Clause 3(xiv) has two limbs and each is answered on its own. The first asks whether the company has an internal audit system commensurate with the size and nature of its business. That is a question about fit, not about section 138 — a company outside the classes section 138 covers still attracts a negative answer if the function it does run is inadequate, and a company inside those classes still fails the limb if the coverage does not match the size and nature of its business. The second limb asks whether the reports of the Internal Auditors for the period under audit were considered by the statutory auditor, which is a statement about what the statutory auditor did. Considering those reports is not the same as adopting them: SA 610 (Revised) governs whether and how the internal audit function's work may be used at all.

citation.ref: paragraph 3(xiv)(a) and 3(xiv)(b)

concepts.subsection: Section 143(1) — Right of access and the duty of inquiry
concepts.statement: Section 143(1) gives every auditor a right of access at all times to the books of account and vouchers of the company, kept at the registered office or elsewhere, and entitles him to require from the officers of the company such information and explanation as he may consider necessary for the performance of his duties. Its proviso then names six matters he shall inquire into: whether loans and advances made on the basis of security have been properly secured and whether the terms on which they have been made are prejudicial to the interests of the company or its members; whether transactions of the company which are represented merely by book entries are prejudicial to the interests of the company; whether so much of the assets of the company as consist of shares, debentures and other securities have been sold at a price less than that at which they were purchased, the company not being an investment company or a banking company; whether loans and advances made by the company have been shown as deposits; whether personal expenses have been charged to revenue account; and, where the books state that shares have been allotted for cash, whether cash has actually been received and, if not, whether the position as stated in the account books and the balance sheet is correct, regular and not misleading. The inquiry is a duty. The reporting is not: nothing is stated on these matters unless the inquiry produces an adverse finding.

citation.ref: Section 143(1) and its proviso, clauses (a) to (f)

concepts.subsection: Section 140(1) — Removal of an auditor before expiry of term
concepts.statement: An auditor appointed under section 139 may be removed from his office before the expiry of his term only by a special resolution of the company, after obtaining the previous approval of the Central Government, and the auditor concerned must be given a reasonable opportunity of being heard before any action is taken. Rule 7 of the Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014 fixes the sequence: the Board passes a resolution; the application to the Central Government goes in Form ADT-2 with the prescribed fee within thirty days of that Board resolution; and the company holds the general meeting to pass the special resolution within sixty days of receiving the Central Government's approval. Approval first, special resolution second — the word in the section is previous approval. None of this is the resignation route under section 140(2), where the auditor leaves of his own motion and files a statement in Form ADT-3 with the company and the Registrar within thirty days.

citation.ref: Section 140(1) with its proviso, read with Rule 7(1), Rule 7(2) and Rule 7(3) of the Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014

concepts.subsection: Second Schedule Part I — Clauses 5, 6, 8 and 9
concepts.statement: Four clauses of Part I of the Second Schedule punish the auditor for what his report does not say. A member in practice is guilty of professional misconduct if he fails to disclose a material fact known to him which is not disclosed in a financial statement, but disclosure of which is necessary in making such financial statement where he is concerned with that financial statement in a professional capacity (Clause 5); if he fails to report a material misstatement known to him to appear in a financial statement with which he is concerned in a professional capacity (Clause 6); if he fails to obtain sufficient information which is necessary for expression of an opinion, or its exceptions are sufficiently material to negate the expression of an opinion (Clause 8); and if he fails to invite attention to any material departure from the generally accepted procedure of audit applicable to the circumstances (Clause 9). Clause 5 is about a fact absent from the statements, Clause 6 about a wrong figure present in them, Clause 8 about the evidence behind the opinion, and Clause 9 about the audit's own method. All four sit in the Second Schedule, which routes the case to the Disciplinary Committee.

citation.ref: Second Schedule, Part I, Clauses 5, 6, 8 and 9

concepts.subsection: SA 210 — Agreeing the Terms of Audit Engagements
concepts.statement: A request to change the terms of an audit engagement is answered by asking why. SA 210 says the auditor shall not agree to a change in the terms of the audit engagement where there is no reasonable justification for doing so. A change in circumstances that affects the entity's requirements, and a misunderstanding as to the nature of the service originally requested, are reasonable justifications. A change sought because the auditor is unable to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence, or because he would otherwise have to modify his opinion, is not — an engagement downgraded to a review so that a qualification disappears is a change with nothing behind it. Where the terms are changed, the auditor and management shall agree on and record the new terms of the engagement in an engagement letter or other suitable form of written agreement. Where the auditor is unable to agree to the change and is not permitted by management to continue the original audit engagement, he withdraws from the engagement where possible under applicable law or regulation, and determines whether there is any obligation, contractual or otherwise, to report the circumstances to other parties, such as those charged with governance, owners or regulators.

citation.ref: para 14, para 16 and para 17

concepts.subsection: SA 220 (Revised) — Quality Management for an Audit
concepts.statement: Overall responsibility for quality does not stop at a signature. SA 220 (Revised) makes the engagement partner responsible for the nature, timing and extent of the direction and supervision of the engagement team and the review of their work, and requires that direction, supervision and review be planned and performed on the basis that the work of less experienced engagement team members is directed, supervised and reviewed by more experienced engagement team members. The partner himself reviews the audit documentation relating to significant matters and significant judgements, including difficult or contentious matters, and the conclusions reached and the basis for them. Before the auditor's report is dated he determines that sufficient appropriate audit evidence has been obtained to support the conclusions reached and for the report to be issued, and where an engagement quality review is required, the report is not dated until he is notified that the review is complete. The extent of the review responds to the nature and circumstances of the engagement — a flat house rule that sends every file through the same review has stopped responding to anything.

citation.ref: the engagement partner's overall responsibility for managing and achieving quality at para 13, with the requirements on direction, supervision and review, on the partner's own review of documentation on significant matters and significant judgements, and on the completion of an engagement quality review before the auditor's report is dated

concepts.subsection: SA 299 (Revised) — Joint Audit of Financial Statements
concepts.statement: Dividing the work does not make joint auditors strangers to each other. SA 299 (Revised) requires that where, in the course of the audit, a joint auditor comes across matters that are relevant to the areas of responsibility of other joint auditors and that deserve their attention, or that require disclosure or require discussion with, or the application of judgement by, other joint auditors, he shall communicate those matters to all the other joint auditors in writing, and shall do so prior to the completion of the audit. On reporting, the joint auditors ordinarily issue a common audit report. Where they are in disagreement with regard to the opinion or any matters to be covered by the audit report, they do not vote: the joint auditor who disagrees expresses his own opinion through a separate audit report, and a joint auditor is not bound by the views of the majority. Coordination is a duty owed in writing to all of them; agreement is not a duty at all.

citation.ref: the coordination requirement to communicate such matters to all the other joint auditors in writing prior to the completion of the audit, and the reporting requirement that a joint auditor in disagreement expresses his opinion in a separate audit report, read with the division of responsibility at para 13 and para 14

concepts.subsection: SA 500 — Audit Evidence
concepts.statement: Appropriateness has two halves, and SA 500 puts both in front of the auditor when procedures are designed. Relevance is the connection between the procedure and the assertion being tested — selecting recorded sales and tracing them outwards tests occurrence, not completeness, and no quantity of that procedure answers the assertion it does not touch. Reliability is influenced by the source and the nature of the evidence, and the standard's generalisations run: evidence from independent sources outside the entity is more reliable than evidence generated internally; internally generated evidence is more reliable where the related controls are effective; evidence obtained directly by the auditor is more reliable than evidence obtained indirectly or by inference; documentary evidence is more reliable than oral; and an original document is more reliable than a photocopy or a facsimile. And where information produced by the entity is used as audit evidence, the auditor evaluates whether it is sufficiently reliable for his purposes — obtaining audit evidence about the accuracy and completeness of the information, and evaluating whether it is sufficiently precise and detailed for those purposes.

citation.ref: para 7 and para 9

concepts.subsection: SA 505 — External Confirmations
concepts.statement: Control of the external confirmation process belongs to the auditor — determining the information to be confirmed, selecting the appropriate confirming party, designing the requests so that they are properly addressed and ask for replies to be sent directly to the auditor, and sending the requests including any follow-up. When management refuses to allow the auditor to send a confirmation request, SA 505 treats the refusal neither as the end of the matter nor as automatically fatal. The auditor inquires as to management's reasons for the refusal and seeks audit evidence as to their validity and reasonableness; evaluates the implications of the refusal on his assessment of the relevant risks of material misstatement, including the risk of fraud, and on the nature, timing and extent of other audit procedures; and performs alternative audit procedures designed to obtain relevant and reliable audit evidence. If he concludes that the refusal is unreasonable, or if the alternative procedures do not produce relevant and reliable audit evidence, he communicates with those charged with governance in accordance with SA 260 and determines the implications for the audit and for the auditor's opinion in accordance with SA 705 (Revised).

citation.ref: para 7, para 8 and para 9

concepts.subsection: SA 540 (Revised) — Auditing Accounting Estimates
concepts.statement: An estimate can be defensible on its own and still be evidence of something. SA 540 (Revised) has the auditor evaluate, based on the audit procedures performed and the audit evidence obtained, whether the accounting estimates and related disclosures are reasonable in the context of the applicable financial reporting framework, or are misstated. It then makes a separate demand: the auditor evaluates whether the judgements and decisions made by management in making the accounting estimates, even if they are individually reasonable, are indicators of possible management bias. A provision set at the low end of a reasonable range, a useful life extended in the year profits fell, an impairment test deferred to the next period — each may pass alone; all of them leaning the same way is the finding. Where indicators of possible management bias are identified, the auditor evaluates the implications for the audit, and where the bias is accompanied by an intention to mislead it is fraudulent in nature and SA 240 follows. Indicators of possible management bias do not themselves constitute misstatements for the purpose of drawing conclusions on the reasonableness of individual accounting estimates.

citation.ref: the overall evaluation of whether the accounting estimates and related disclosures are reasonable or are misstated, and the separate evaluation of whether management's judgements and decisions are indicators of possible management bias, read with the retrospective review at para 14

concepts.subsection: SA 700 (Revised) — Forming an Opinion and Reporting
concepts.statement: Before the report is written the opinion has to be formed, and SA 700 sets out what forming it involves. The auditor concludes whether he has obtained reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements as a whole are free from material misstatement, taking into account whether sufficient appropriate audit evidence has been obtained under SA 330 and whether uncorrected misstatements are material individually or in aggregate under SA 450. He then evaluates whether the financial statements are prepared, in all material respects, in accordance with the requirements of the applicable financial reporting framework — an evaluation that includes consideration of the qualitative aspects of the entity's accounting practices, including indicators of possible bias in management's judgements. Specifically he evaluates whether the financial statements adequately disclose the significant accounting policies selected and applied; whether those policies are consistent with the framework and are appropriate; whether accounting estimates made by management are reasonable; whether the information presented is relevant, reliable, comparable and understandable; whether adequate disclosures enable users to understand the effect of material transactions and events; and whether the terminology used, including the title of each financial statement, is appropriate. Where the framework is a fair presentation framework, he also evaluates whether the financial statements achieve fair presentation.

citation.ref: para 11 to para 15

concepts.subsection: SA 706 (Revised) — Emphasis of Matter and Other Matter Paragraphs
concepts.statement: An Emphasis of Matter paragraph is available only where two gates are passed. The auditor includes one to draw users' attention to a matter presented or disclosed in the financial statements that is, in his judgement, of such importance that it is fundamental to users' understanding of the financial statements — provided the auditor would not be required to modify the opinion in accordance with SA 705 (Revised) as a result of that matter, and provided that, where SA 701 applies, the matter has not been determined to be a key audit matter to be communicated in the auditor's report. The second gate governs an Other Matter paragraph too, which is additionally unavailable where law or regulation prohibits it. When an Emphasis of Matter paragraph is included it sits in a separate section of the report under a heading including the term "Emphasis of Matter"; it carries a clear reference to the matter being emphasised and to where the relevant disclosures that fully describe it can be found in the financial statements; it refers only to information presented or disclosed in the financial statements; and it states that the auditor's opinion is not modified in respect of the matter. A widespread use of such paragraphs diminishes the effectiveness of the auditor's communication of those matters.

citation.ref: para 8(a) and para 8(b), with the content and placement requirements in para 9

concepts.subsection: SA 720 — The Auditor's Responsibilities Relating to Other Information
concepts.statement: Reading the other information is the start; SA 720 then says what happens when the reading turns something up. Where a material inconsistency appears to exist, or the other information otherwise appears to be materially misstated, the auditor discusses the matter with management and, if necessary, performs other procedures to conclude whether a material misstatement of the other information exists, a material misstatement of the financial statements exists, or the auditor's understanding of the entity and its environment needs to be updated. Where he concludes that a material misstatement of the other information exists, he requests management to correct it; if management agrees he determines that the correction has been made, and if management refuses he communicates the matter with those charged with governance and requests that the correction be made. Where the other information was obtained before the date of the auditor's report and remains uncorrected, the auditor takes appropriate action, including considering the implications for the auditor's report and communicating with those charged with governance about how he plans to address the material misstatement in it, or withdrawing from the engagement where withdrawal is possible under applicable law or regulation. Where the uncorrected other information was obtained after the date of the report, he takes appropriate action to seek to have the matter appropriately addressed, which may include obtaining legal advice.

citation.ref: para 16 to para 19

concepts.subsection: SA 810 — Engagements to Report on Summary Financial Statements
concepts.statement: Summary financial statements are derived from audited financial statements and contain less detail, while still providing a structured representation of the entity's economic resources or obligations at a point in time, or of the changes in them for a period. SA 810 will not let an auditor report on them unless he has been engaged to conduct an audit, in accordance with the Standards on Auditing, of the financial statements from which they are derived — a summary cannot be reported on by someone who never audited the source. Acceptance also turns on the applied criteria being acceptable and on management agreeing its responsibilities, including making the audited financial statements available to the intended users. The opinion is not an audit opinion on the summary in its own right: it says either that the summary financial statements are consistent, in all material respects, with the audited financial statements in accordance with the applied criteria, or that they are a fair summary of the audited financial statements in accordance with the applied criteria. The report states that the summary financial statements do not contain all the disclosures required by the financial reporting framework applied in the preparation of the audited financial statements, and that reading them is not a substitute for reading the audited financial statements. It identifies the audited financial statements and the date of the auditor's report on them, and where that report carried a modified opinion, an Emphasis of Matter or an Other Matter paragraph, or a material uncertainty related to going concern, the report on the summary says so. It is not dated earlier than the auditor's report on the audited financial statements.

citation.ref: the precondition that the auditor has been engaged to audit the financial statements from which the summary financial statements are derived, the two permitted forms of opinion — consistency in all material respects, or a fair summary — and the required statements about the omitted disclosures and about reading the audited financial statements

concepts.subsection: SAE 3402 — Assurance Reports on Controls at a Service Organisation
concepts.statement: Where a service organisation itself uses a subservice organisation, the description of its system deals with that subservice organisation by one of two methods, and the service auditor's report follows the choice. Under the inclusive method the description includes the nature of the services provided by the subservice organisation together with its relevant control objectives and related controls, and the service auditor's procedures — and his opinion — extend to those controls. Under the carve-out method the description identifies the nature of the services performed by the subservice organisation but excludes its control objectives and related controls, and the service auditor's procedures do not extend to them; the report then covers the service organisation's own controls alone, and a user auditor has to obtain assurance about the carved-out controls elsewhere. A carve-out is a permitted presentation, not a modification of the opinion. SAE 3402 also requires a written assertion by the service organisation about the fair presentation of the description, the suitability of the design of the controls and, in a type 2 report, their operating effectiveness throughout the specified period; where the service organisation will not provide it, the service auditor does not accept or continue the engagement unless law or regulation requires otherwise. The service auditor must be independent of the service organisation; he is not required to be independent of the user entities.

citation.ref: the inclusive and carve-out methods of dealing with a subservice organisation in the description of the system, and the service organisation's written assertion on the fair presentation of the description, the suitability of the design of the controls and, in a type 2 report, their operating effectiveness

concepts.subsection: SAE 3400 — The Examination of Prospective Financial Information
concepts.statement: Prospective financial information is financial information based on assumptions about events that may occur in the future and possible actions by an entity. A forecast is prepared on the basis of best-estimate assumptions as to events management expects to take place and the actions it expects to take. A projection is prepared on the basis of hypothetical assumptions about future events and management actions that are not necessarily expected to take place, or on a mixture of best-estimate and hypothetical assumptions. Because the information relates to events that have not occurred and may not occur, the auditor is not in a position to express an opinion as to whether the results shown will be achieved. SAE 3400 has him express negative assurance as to whether the assumptions provide a reasonable basis for the prospective financial information, and an opinion as to whether it is properly prepared on the basis of those assumptions and is presented in accordance with the relevant financial reporting framework — with a caveat that actual results are likely to be different from the prospective financial information, since anticipated events frequently do not occur as expected and the variation may be material. The auditor should not accept, or should withdraw from, an engagement where the assumptions are clearly unrealistic or where he believes the prospective financial information will be inappropriate for its intended use.

citation.ref: the definitions of a forecast and of a projection, the negative assurance on whether the assumptions provide a reasonable basis together with the opinion on preparation and presentation, and the circumstances in which the engagement should not be accepted

concepts.subsection: SRS 4400 — Engagements to Perform Agreed-upon Procedures
concepts.statement: An agreed-upon procedures engagement carries no assurance of any kind. The practitioner performs procedures of an audit nature to which he, the entity and any appropriate third parties have agreed, and reports the factual findings — what he did and what he found — leaving the users to assess those procedures and findings for themselves and to draw their own conclusions. Because the report means something only to those who know what was agreed, its distribution is restricted to the parties that have agreed to the procedures, and the report says so. The report of factual findings sets out the purpose and the agreed procedures in enough detail for a reader to understand the nature and extent of the work performed; states that the procedures performed were those agreed with the recipient; identifies the specific financial or non-financial information to which they were applied; states that the engagement was performed in accordance with SRS 4400; and states that it does not constitute an audit or a review and that accordingly no assurance is expressed. Independence is not a requirement for an agreed-upon procedures engagement; where the terms or objectives of the engagement, or national standards, require it, that requirement governs, and where the practitioner is not independent a statement to that effect is made in the report of factual findings.

citation.ref: the elements of the report of factual findings, the statement that no assurance is expressed, the restriction of distribution to the parties that have agreed to the procedures, and the position that independence is not a requirement with a statement to be made where the practitioner is not independent

concepts.subsection: Section 139(2) — Rotation of auditors
concepts.statement: Rotation is a limit on tenure, not a comment on performance. No listed company, and no company belonging to the classes of companies prescribed under the Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014, shall appoint or re-appoint an individual as auditor for more than one term of five consecutive years, or an audit firm as auditor for more than two terms of five consecutive years. An individual who has completed his term is not eligible for re-appointment as auditor in the same company for five years from the completion of that term, and a firm that has completed two terms is not eligible for re-appointment as auditor in the same company for five years from the completion of those terms. The bar reaches past the outgoing firm itself: as on the date of appointment, no audit firm having a common partner or partners with the outgoing audit firm, whose tenure has expired in a company immediately preceding the financial year, shall be appointed as auditor of the same company for a period of five years. Rotation runs against the company, so a firm barred in one company may audit any other. And section 139(3) lets the members resolve, if they wish, that the audit partner and his team shall be rotated at such intervals as they may resolve, or that the audit shall be conducted by more than one auditor.

citation.ref: Section 139(2) with its provisos on ineligibility for re-appointment for five years and on a firm having a common partner with the outgoing audit firm, read with section 139(3)

concepts.subsection: Sections 145 and 146 — Signing the report and attending the general meeting
concepts.statement: Two short sections say who signs and who has to be in the room. Under section 145 the person appointed as auditor of the company shall sign the auditor's report, or sign or certify any other document of the company, in accordance with section 141(2) — under which, where a firm including a limited liability partnership is appointed as auditor, only the partners who are chartered accountants shall be authorised to act and sign on behalf of the firm. Section 145 then requires that the qualifications, observations or comments on financial transactions or matters which have any adverse effect on the functioning of the company, mentioned in the auditor's report, shall be read before the company in general meeting and shall be open to inspection by any member of the company. Section 146 requires that all notices of, and other communications relating to, any general meeting be forwarded to the auditor, and that the auditor shall, unless otherwise exempted by the company, attend any general meeting either himself or through his authorised representative, who shall also be qualified to be an auditor; and it gives him the right to be heard at that meeting on any part of the business which concerns him as the auditor. The right to be heard is bounded by that phrase — it is not a general right to address the meeting.

citation.ref: Section 145 read with section 141(2), and section 146

concepts.subsection: CARO 2020 — Clause 3(xviii)
concepts.statement: Clause 3(xviii) makes the incoming auditor report on the exit of the last one.
